chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Aban, from Al-Wassafi, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Revere your elders, and maintain ties with your relatives, and you do not maintain ties with them with anything better than refraining from causing them harm.'
ai.seo_question: What is the best way to maintain ties with relatives according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the concept of *silat al-rahim* (maintaining kinship) by defining its essence not merely through material gifts, but through the spiritual and ethical discipline of refraining from causing distress (*kaff al-adha*) to elders. This aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and the preservation of social harmony, where the absence of friction is often considered a more profound act of piety than outward displays of generosity. The narration underscores the practical application of kinship rights within the family structure, reflecting the broader Islamic principle that good character is the true measure of faith.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Aban, from Al Wassafy who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Revere your elderly, and have goodly relations with your relatives, and you will not be helping them with anything more superior than stopping the harm from them’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd Allah ibn Aban from al-Wassafi who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Consider your grown up people as great and maintain good relations with relatives. No other way is better to maintain good relations with relatives than keeping all troubles away from them.’”
